context: Each move climbs 1 or 2 stairs. Landing on a stair incurs its cost. In the diagram, n labels the stair and cost[n] its cost. The ground has starting cost cost[0]=0. The goal is to land on stair 3 and pay its cost.
description: Below the stairs, the numbers n=0, 1, 2, 3 align with the costs cost[n]=0, 1, 10, 1. The tread of stair 2 and its cost of 10 are red. The tread of the target stair, 3, is green. Above the stairs, a solid teal line traces 0→1→2→3, a dotted blue line traces 0→2→3, and a dashed orange line traces 0→1→3. The note below lists these three routes and identifies 0→1→3 as the cheapest, with cost 2.

The table uses the individual stair costs shown in the diagram. The calculations and the totals 12 and 11 come from adding the costs of the stairs visited. The original diagram does not label these two totals.

frames.explanation: Both of the first two routes visit stair 2, which costs 10. Only 0→1→3 skips it, giving the lowest cost.
frames.title: Minimum cost to climb three stairs

summary: The costs for the ground and stairs 1 through 3 are 0, 1, 10, and 1. Route 0→1→3 skips stair 2, which costs 10, and achieves the minimum total cost of 2.

tables.caption: Costs of the three routes (calculated from the stair costs shown)

title: Minimum cost to climb three stairs
